newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures reversed part of Thursday's losses to go into a long-weekend in France slightly higher while the franc benefitted from a slide in the mark against the dollar and other European currencies.
Traders said reassuring words about monetary union from Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet buoyed sentiment and provided an excuse for buying even though he said little new.

After the initial rally, the September contract traded in a subdued range until a decline in U.S. June producer price figures sparked a brief spike higher. However the higher prices simply attracted profit-taking ahead of the weekend.
Some traders did not rule out a continuation of the rise in U.S. bonds and said that this could prompt a correction higher when the French market opens for trading again on Tuesday.

Stuart Thomson, chief market economist at Credit Agricole Indosuez, said benign U.S. inflation figures were unlikely to have a major positive impact on bonds and investors were focusing more on activity in the consumer sector.
"There's nothing new about a drop in U.S. PPI these days. It's not going to make the (Federal Reserve) cut rates and since not going to make them raise rates it's less important," he said.
"If (U.S. retail sales figures) are well behaved the curve will continue to flatten," Thomson said.

Analysts and traders said the German government's announcement that its 1997 budget deficit plans predicted a gap amounting to three percent of gross domestic product had little impact as few believed the politicians.

"They'll always keep three percent as a political target and the markets just accept they will overshoot," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance said. "It's too confusing to trade on."

"I'm sceptical because with all the numbers we had in May and June it suggested the overshoot might by enormous and now, miraculously, it's all settled without a severe tax increase," he said. "Maybe the problem was a bit less severe, but I still cannot see how they'll get to three percent."
The French franc climbed with other European currencies against the mark as the German unit slumped to a six-year low versus the U.S. dollar.
The franc climbed as high as 3.3760 per mark from an early low of 3.3823 but slipped as low as 5.9883 against the dollar, its lowest level since February 1994.
